transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-27 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Samir (Redwood CSM), Alex (Citrine Head of ML), Priya (Citrine Platform), Connor (Citrine Product), Marta (Finance), Diego (Security)

Summary: quick QBR-style health check focused on near-term budget forecasting, service guardrails, and feasibility of a private deployment pilot. Discussed patterns in latency/cost, trade-offs (hosted vs dedicated vs private), and required artifacts for next-phase pilot.

Topics: usage trends, cost drivers, SLA targets, security/compliance checklist, pilot scope, timelines

--- Transcript body ---
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we know it's a lot of folks. I'll kick us off, quick agenda: usage/cost snapshot, reliability notes, then Jordan will walk through private pilot feasibility and what we need from Citrine. Then recp and action items, okay?
[00:12] Alex Romero: Sounds good, thanks Maya. We wanted to use this time to make sure the budgets we carved out for Q1 actually map to the traffic we see, and then figure out what level of guardrails we need so product doesn't spike costs.
[00:20] Priya Das: +1 also a big ask from infra is clarity on network egress and VPC peering for private deploy, and a list of firewall ports.
[00:28] Jordan Kim: Great, I'll cover that in the second half. To start, Samir will show the high-level metric set, then we can dig into cost buckets. Samir?
[00:35] Samir Venkatar: Sure I'll share my screen — give me a sec — okay pulled up the last 90 days. The main signals: median latency at p50 is 110ms for the hosted model, p95 around 420ms. Token mix is 60% embeddings, 30% short-chat/generation (<=128 tokens), 10% long context generation. The big cost driver is repeated small calls — high per-request overhead — and a small percentage of heavy fine-tuning style workloads.
[01:02] Priya Das: Hmm that aligns, we do have a bursty endpoint for 'product-summarize' which is chatty. Any recommended knobs?
[01:08] Jordan Kim: Two levers: batching at the SDK layer and prefix caching (KV cache) for repeated contexts. Redwood Optimize can suggest batching windows; for quick wins, set client-side batching 50–200ms and enable KV cache for the summarize route. You will trade micro-latency for throughput so test in staging.
[01:25] Connor Lee: When you say trade micro-latency, how much? Product owners need a number.
[01:29] Jordan Kim: Based on similar customers, expect p50 to degrade by ~20–40ms but p95 may improve because we avoid token amplification on concurrency — net cost reduction 20–35% depending on request shape. Those are estimates; we'll produce a tailored forecast.
[01:45] Marta Silva: From finance perspective we need a worst-case and best-case for Q1. Can Redwood provide a conservative and optimistic scenario?
[01:50] Maya Patel: Yes, that's in the next steps — we'll send a cost workbook with three scenarios (hosted baseline, dedicated reserved capacity, and private pilot). Assumptions will include token histograms, burst percentiles, and quantization settings.
[02:05] Diego Alvarez: Quick security note — Citrine requires SOC2 Type II, SAML SSO, and KMS-backed key management for any private deployment. Do you support customer-managed KMS?
[02:12] Jordan Kim: We do. For Private we integrate with AWS KMS/HSM or in on-prem cases we can do an HSM-backed key. Audit logs are available and can be forwarded to your SIEM. For hosted, we offer encryption at rest and managed keys, but for our private package customers can bring their own keys.
[02:28] Diego Alvarez: And audit log retention? We need 12 months immutable.
[02:31] Maya Patel: We can support 12 months as part of an enterprise package, will note that as a requirement.
[02:36] Alex Romero: On reliability — last month we saw two transient increases in 5xx when we had cache-stamping on a new model variant. Was that on Redwood side or our client?
[02:45] Jordan Kim: Looks like both. There was a model rollout that increased memory pressure on the node pool, causing GC and temporary higher 5xx. We recommended a canary rollout with smaller shard size and pre-warm caches — Redwood Console has rollout controls for canary and automatic fallback.
[03:01] Priya Das: Pre-warm caches — can you automate that for us?
[03:04] Jordan Kim: Yes, we have an endpoint for warm/cold priming and we can include a warm-up job in the rollout plan. We'll provide a runbook.
[03:10] Connor Lee: For the private pilot — what's the minimum capacity and timeline? We're thinking pilot with 1–2 GPU nodes to validate latency and correctness.
[03:18] Jordan Kim: Minimum viable private pilot is typically a 2-GPU setup for HA; one GPU is possible but we lose redundancy. Timeline is about 6–8 weeks from kickoff for a VPC-based private deployment if networking and KMS are straightforward. If Citrine prefers an on-prem air-gapped install, add 2–4 weeks for packaging and HSM configuration.
[03:36] Alex Romero: Budget-wise, how should we compare dedicated reserved capacity vs private? We need to justify to finance.
[03:42] Maya Patel: High-level: hosted is Opex at per-token, easiest to start. Dedicated reserved gives a lower unit cost but requires commitment and can be cheaper at scale. Private has higher fixed setup and infra cost but gives control (data residency, KMS). We'll model per-token TCO including infra, network egress, and ops headcount.
[03:58] Marta Silva: Ops headcount — estimate? For private on-prem we might need a 0.5–1 FTE to run it?
[04:04] Jordan Kim: Typically customers allocate 0.25–0.5 FTE for private if Redwood handles most infra automation, more if you want deep custom ops. We'll make a conservative assumption in the workbook.
[04:14] Priya Das: Network-wise, what ports and patterns? We use strict egress controls; need an explicit list.
[04:20] Jordan Kim: We'll send a network checklist: outbound TLS to Redwood control plane (list of IPs), VPC peering steps, and ports – mostly 443 plus ephemeral ports for model shard comms if using private with multi-node.
[04:31] Diego Alvarez: Is data plane traffic kept in VPC? We need assurance that inference payloads don't transit public internet.
[04:36] Jordan Kim: In private deployment, yes data plane stays in customer VPC; for hosted it's encrypted and traverses our managed endpoints. We'll provide a network diagram.
[04:45] Alex Romero: We also want to quantize some of our workloads. How much throughput gain do you see on 4-bit quantization?
[04:51] Jordan Kim: For many decoder-style models, 4-bit int8-like quantization gets 1.8x–2.5x throughput improvement and reduces memory footprint, but quality can vary. Redwood Optimize will run a small eval on your prompt set to estimate quality delta. We'll include that in the pilot scope.
[05:05] Priya Das: About SLAs — our SLAs are strict: 99.9% uptime and sub-500ms p95 for inference. Are those realistic for hosted?
[05:12] Maya Patel: Hosted SLA is typically 99.9% but p95 depends on model and seq length. For strict p95 targets we recommend dedicated capacity or private to get predictable tail latencies. We can attach an SLA to Dedicated with tail latency SLOs baked in, and rollback policies.
[05:28] Connor Lee: If we go dedicated, can we burst to higher capacity for Black Friday-style events?
[05:33] Jordan Kim: Yes — dedicated can be configured with burst pools if you want ephemeral scale. That affects pricing. We'll show the costing tradeoff in the workbook.
[05:41] Samir Venkatar: Quick note on usage anomalies — we saw a 12% week-over-week increase in token usage when the marketing team launched a campaign. Consider per-route quotas or rate limits to avoid surprise bills.
[05:52] Alex Romero: Good call. We need guardrails so marketing can't accidentally blast prod.
[05:56] Maya Patel: Redwood Console supports per-route quotas, token budgets, and alerts. We can propose a default quota profile for Citrine and a staged escalation policy.
[06:06] Marta Silva: Can you give an example of how that looks financially? Like a cost cap and notification at 80%?
[06:10] Maya Patel: Yes — we'll include recommended thresholds: soft limit at 70% spends with webhook alerts, hard limit at 95% with automatic throttle. We'll model the financial impact in the scenarios.
[06:20] Priya Das: One last technical question — model rollbacks: if a rollout fails, is there automatic fallback to previous model?
[06:26] Jordan Kim: Yes we support canary rollouts with automatic health checks and instant rollback to the last known-good model if error rates cross threshold. You can configure rollback criteria in the Console.
[06:34] Diego Alvarez: About legal/compliance: we have a vendor questionnaire. Will you fill it?
[06:38] Maya Patel: Yes — Diego, we'll send the Redwood security pack and SOC2 report. If you want we can do a follow-up security review call with our security lead.
[06:46] Diego Alvarez: Please do. Also will need proof of encryption for logs.
[06:49] Jordan Kim: Logs are encrypted at rest and can be forwarded to your SIEM over TLS; we can enable log redaction and PII filters.
[06:56] Alex Romero: Recap?
[06:58] Maya Patel: Sure recap quick: 1) Redwood to send cost workbook with three scenarios by 2026-02-02; 2) Citrine to export token histogram and top endpoints (Priya) by 2026-02-03; 3) Jordan to run private deployment checklist and schedule pilot kickoff call for 2026-02-09; 4) Diego to share vendor questionnaire items by 2026-02-05. Anything else?
[07:18] Priya Das: Also please include example network config and firewall list.
[07:21] Jordan Kim: On it, will include network checklist and diagram.
[07:25] Connor Lee: We'll review the workbook and then decide between dedicated vs hosted ramp vs private pilot.
[07:29] Maya Patel: Great. Samir anything else from metrics side?
[07:31] Samir Venkatar: No that's it — I'll attach the 90-day CSV in the email.
[07:35] Alex Romero: Thanks everyone, that was helpful.
[07:37] Maya Patel: Thanks all.
